subject: Temporary SLA routing & on-call exemption request — Finmark maintenance window
messages:
From: Jared Ellison <jared.ellison@finmark.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finmark.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 22:14:00 -0700
Subject: Scheduled maintenanceTonight — request for temporary SLA routing adjustments

Marcus,

Heads up: Finmark has a scheduled database maintenance window tonight (Oct 4, 01:00–04:00 UTC) that will briefly impact our real-time traffic to hosted endpoints. Our SREs expect a ~10–15 minute rolling disruption during failover (we've accounted for retries on our side), but because this overlaps with our peak ETL batch we wanted to request temporary changes to response-time SLO handling for the affected window.

Specifically: we need a short-term allowance for P2 response timing (extend to 2 hours for alerts triggered during the window) and a fallback routing option to a dedicated route (if available) to avoid throttling. Can Redwood confirm whether you can: 
- Enable fallback to our Dedicated pool (if capacity permits) for 01:00–04:00 UTC
- Temporarily mark incidents from Finmark during that window as exempt from P2 SLA breach penalties

I realize this is an operational ask on short notice — we can run rollbacks quickly if you need. Jared

--
Jared Ellison
Platform Ops, Finmark
[jared.ellison@finmark.com]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jared Ellison <jared.ellison@finmark.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finmark.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 00:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduled maintenanceTonight — request for temporary SLA routing adjustments

Jared — thanks for the heads-up and the clear ask. Short answer: we can support a temporary operational change, but I need a couple of confirmations and approvals before we flip anything in prod. Proposed approach below.

What we need from Finmark:
- Exact UTC window you want us to consider (you mentioned 01:00–04:00) — please confirm in a follow-up.
- Expected request volume delta during the window and which endpoints are critical (list path prefixes).

Proposed Redwood changes (subject to internal approval):
1) Temporary routing: route Finmark traffic to the Dedicated pool for the 01:00–04:00 UTC window (fall back to hosted afterwards). This requires capacity check; if Dedicated is at cap we will instead provision burst nodes in us-west.
2) SLA labeling: for incidents that originate within the confirmed window and are caused by Finmark-side maintenance, we can mark P2 incidents as "maintenance-exempt" to avoid automatic billing/penalty triggers. This is an operational metadata flag in the incident record.
3) Escalation path tweak: during the window we will route P1s to the on-call SRE first, then escalate immediately to Dev Lead (Dev Patel) if the incident persists past 15 minutes. For P2s, the first responder will be Support L2 (Rachel Kim).

I will need approval from Rachel (Support) and Dev (on-call policy) to proceed. If approved, I will:
- Create SUP-4321 and attach a short runbook patch
- Push a one-off routing rule and the exemption flag
- Share post-window incident summary and metrics (latency, error-rate, token cost delta)

If that plan looks OK, confirm the exact window and critical paths and we will queue this for the 01:00 UTC change.

—Marcus

Marcus Lin
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
[m: +1 (415) 555-0199]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Ellison <jared.ellison@finmark.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@finmark.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Scheduled maintenanceTonight — request for temporary SLA routing adjustments

Team — forwarding Finmark's maintenance window request. Key points: they want Dedicated fallback and P2 SLA exemption for the confirmed window (01:00–04:00 UTC).

Action items I need from you both this morning before I send final confirmation to Finmark: 
- Rachel: confirm Support L2 coverage and that marking incidents "maintenance-exempt" is acceptable from a CS/contract perspective. If not, suggest wording for the exemption.
- Dev: confirm on-call SRE availability for escalation (P1 escalation to you at 15 minutes) and whether we can provision burst nodes in us-west if Dedicated is saturated.

I have a short patch to the runbook (attached) and an escalation matrix spreadsheet that maps who gets paged at each threshold. If we approve, I'll open SUP-4321 and request a targeted routing rule at 00:50 UTC to take effect at 01:00 UTC.

Attachments: [Attachment: runbook_v2.pdf (PDF, 183KB)] [Attachment: escalation_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)]

Thanks — Marcus

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Ellison <jared.ellison@finmark.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@finmark.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Scheduled maintenanceTonight — request for temporary SLA routing adjustments

Marcus — reviewed. Support side is OK with the temporary exemption under the following conditions:
1) Finmark confirms the exact UTC window (01:00–04:00 UTC) in writing (reply-all with confirmation).
2) Finmark agrees to a post-window incident review within 48 hours (we'll share the metric delta).
3) The exemption applies only to customer-caused maintenance events where Finmark has notified + acknowledged the window.

Dev Patel has confirmed on-call escalation: he will be on standby and will accept P1 escalations after 15 minutes. If Dedicated capacity is full, we will provision burst nodes in us-west — Rachel asked SRE to prioritize minimal-impact provisioning (no restarts of existing pools).

I'll approve the routing rule and the incident metadata exemption once Jared confirms the window here. Marcus — please create SUP-4321, attach the runbook patch, and set the routing rule to expire at 04:05 UTC to capture slow drains.

Rachel Kim
Head of Support, Redwood Inference
[rachel_kim@redwood.com]
